## **What Is AI Clothes Changing?**


**AI clothes changing** replaces visible clothing in a photo. In Magic Hour Clothes Changer, the person photo and clothing item are separate image inputs. Choose which part of the outfit should change, then generate a visual mockup. A prompt-based image editor is another route when you want to describe a local change instead of supplying a garment image.


Processing time depends on the chosen tool, model, image, and queue. Inspect the result rather than treating a fixed completion-time promise as a guarantee.


This type of editing is useful for social media content, fashion concepts, profile photos, marketing materials, and creative projects. It is similar to how an image editor uses AI to modify visual elements without requiring advanced skills.


## **What You Need Before You Start**


Before changing clothes in a photo with AI, make sure you have the following:


- A clear photo of one main person that you own or have permission to edit
- A clothing image you may use, or an available garment preset
- A supported browser; for the signed-in Create workflow below, a Magic Hour account with enough credits for the displayed estimate


You do not need Photoshop or specialist design software. The garment reference is required for this workflow; if you only have a written instruction, use AI Image Editor.


Magic Hour works entirely in your browser, so you can use it on a desktop, laptop, tablet, or phone. If you're editing on the go, this also works on your phone browser, with no app needed.


## **Why Use AI Instead of Manual Photo Editing?**


Traditional photo editing requires selecting clothing areas, masking objects, adjusting shadows, and matching colors. For most people, that process takes time and often requires professional software.


AI simplifies the first mockup: provide the person and garment images, choose the swap scope, then review the generated result. You still need to check identity, proportions and the parts that should remain unchanged. This is useful for exploring outfit ideas before further editing.


If you want to edit more than clothing later, Magic Hour also offers an[AI Image Editor](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-image-editor) that can modify other parts of an image.

## Step 2: Upload the Person and Clothing Images, Then Set Swap Type


Put the source portrait in Person Image and the garment reference in Clothing Item Image. Both are required. The available presets can supply a person or clothing item, but check which input you are selecting before generating.


For the best results, use a clear photo where the person's clothing is fully visible and the lighting is good. Photos with a front-facing pose and minimal obstructions generally give the AI more information to work with, helping it generate more realistic outfit changes.


Choose Entire Outfit for the principal outfit, Upper Body for a shirt, jacket or sweater, or Lower Body for pants, shorts or a skirt. Use the narrowest scope that matches the task. Entire Outfit does not guarantee replacement of shoes, belts, jewelry, bags or every accessory. There is no control here for selecting one person in a group photo.

Review both image inputs, Swap Type, model, resolution and the displayed credit estimate. Select Generate Image. The model attempts to adapt the garment to the source pose and lighting; compare the output with both inputs rather than assuming every design detail stays exact.

It is creating a new version that attempts to match the lighting, body position, folds, and proportions of the original photo, which helps the clothing look more realistic.

When the generation is complete, review the output and compare it with your original image. If you're happy with the result, use the download option to save the edited version to your device.

## **Tips for the Best Results**


- Use a clear, high-resolution photo with good lighting. Images where the clothing is fully visible typically produce more consistent results.
- Choose photos where the subject is facing the camera or standing in a natural pose. This helps the AI better understand how the outfit should fit the body.
- Compare different garment references with the same person photo. Keep the source and swap scope consistent so you can see what each clothing choice changes.
- Avoid blurry photos, heavily cropped images, or photos where clothing is hidden behind objects, as these can reduce accuracy.
